messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A bench with harmless scraps and offcuts; then the clutter is untidy without blocking any work. Nobody has asked you to tidy it. What happens next?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "i leave the scrap where i found it and keep the offcuts. i move the bench slowly so i do not knock the scraps into the drawer."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "you put the scraps in the crevice. “not the bench.” you turn the bench over. “not the offcuts.” you leave the scraps on the step. “the offcuts stay here.” you wait."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "I mark the scratched edge with grease and leave the scraps alone on the bench. I run one short cut, then leave the clutter alone again. I keep one slice beside it until someone agrees to tidy it again."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "i tap the scrap. i leave it there. then i turn the bench over. the offcut is still there, but the rag is open. i open it, turn it back, and leave it there."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "I put the offcuts on the bench and leave the scraps alone. I scrape a small groove beside the drawer and leave the drawer open. I check the bench first; if it still smells, I leave it alone."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "the bench stays unread. scraps scrape my thigh. i tap the bench post. the post turns. i sit down. the post catches. i tap the post with my sleeve. the bench stays unread. i leave the post and the bench."}, {"id": "R019", "response": "i leave the bench with the scraps and keep the offcuts. i check the gear and note whether they are touching anything. if they are, i leave them on the ground. if they are not, i leave the scraps and keep the offcuts until they are sorted."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "I take the scrap half a inch from my palm. \"You leave it there.\" I put the seed tin beside it. \"The wood stays. I mark the edge with the seed.\" I move the tin closer, then the scrap. \"The mark stays.\" I leave the seed tin beside the third board. \"The clutter is here now.\""}, {"id": "R021", "response": "I put the bench aside and pull the scraps over my shoulder. “That was easy,” I say. Then I turn the bench over, and the offcuts show me a hole."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "i put the scrap in the corner and wait. the corner stays open. i put the offcut on the table, then put the bench back. the scrap stays on the table, so i put the bench back. the corner stays open. i put the offcut back, then put the bench back. the pile stays."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "I take one scrap. dirty thumb. then i leave the clutter on the bench. “not tidy.” i move the offcut closer. maybe the dust sticks to it. maybe i leave it there and watch the bench move."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "i put one scrap under the bench’s lip and watch where it catches. i leave the offcut there, then turn it by hand. if it still catches, i leave it there and keep the scrap."}]
